newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican Zapatista backers tell Clinton to go home.
newsitem.headline: Mexican Zapatista backers tell Clinton to go home.
newsitem.dateline: SAN CRISTOBAL DE LAS CASAS, Mexico 1997-05-04

text.p: Supporters of Mexico's Zapatista guerrillas sent a message to President Bill Clinton on Sunday that he was not welcome in Mexico, linking him to Mexican government repression.
Clinton was due to arrive in Mexico on Monday for his first official visit here. First Lady Hillary Clinton arrived in Mexico's Yucatan peninsula on Sunday night.

The Committee of Indigenous Political Prisoners also denounced a Mexican government decision to expel 12 European human rights workers based in the southern state of Chiapas, centre of the Zapatista uprising more than three years ago.
Eleven of the 12 are contesting their expulsion in court.

"We ask President Bill Clinton not to visit our country; he is not welcome, and we call on all of our Mexican brothers to oppose receiving those who only kill and humiliate," protest leader Manuel Perez said in a statement issued in Tuxtla Gutierrez, the capital of Chiapas state.
The group staged a weeklong protest in front of the main government offices in Tuxtla Gutierrez, camping out there since last Monday.

They said they brought Clinton into the protest because he supports an austere "neoliberal" economic programme in Mexico as well as the militarization of Mexico's war on drugs, which they claim is a cover to forcefully crack down on dissent.
Chiapas, among the poorest states in Mexico, has been in turmoil since the predominantly Maya Indian Zapatista National Liberation Army (EZLN) launched its uprising on Jan. 1, 1994.

Combat with the Mexican army was brief, and the two sides are at an impasse in drawn-out peace talks. But in the meantime, violent clashes between protesters and police have become common in Chiapas, as have attacks by paramilitary groups allegedly representing landed interests.

The leftist Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD) said on Sunday that one of its Chiapas candidates for Congress was stopped by the "Peace and Justice" paramilitary group and shot in the abdomen in an attempt to intimidate him.

The European human rights workers in Chiapas said Mexico ordered them to leave the country because they were here only on tourist visas. It is the third time in the past two weeks Mexico has kicked out foreign human rights workers for that reason. A ruling on their court challenge was due on Monday.
